analysis: Both units are base-side text of docs/provider/cli-reference.md. The PR changes are documentation only: the 'Last updated' date at line 3, a new `addon` subcommand table row after line 155, and a new `darkbloom addon` section after roughly line 903 (status/hold/release of add-on holds via the provider's owner-only lifecycle mailbox bound to live process identity). The head-side addon section and the patch excerpt are truncated, so I could not review the full addon text. Existing base content on logout (lines 542-581), switch (314-396), the encrypted SSD cache (66-88), and attestation/enroll is unchanged by this diff. I found no regression from the docs. Threat-model gaps that remain unverified and need the code and addon-hold.md, addon-hold-ipc.md and AddonCommand.swift (not supplied): (1) the add-on hold IPC is a new local attack surface (local socket plus lifecycle mailbox) with possible same-user process abuse, and a hold could cause denial of service or a stalled drain (TB-003, T-010); (2) whether add-on VMs touch decrypted prompt memory, the cache, or the serving authorization boundary (A-001, TB-007, TB-011); (3) whether a hold interacts with graceful drain and stop semantics. No threat model entry covers this feature, so the model likely needs a new trust boundary or threat entry once the implementation lands. I cannot assess the implementation from documentation alone, so I request deeper review of the code paths that accompany this PR.
